item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 282311
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fausto, located in the Central Pacific a few hundred miles
east-northeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Genevieve,
located several hundred miles southwest of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Public Advisory Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Tue Jul 28 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 290232
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
500 PM HST Tue Jul 28 2026
 
...MAJOR HURRICANE GENEVIEVE MOVING WEST-NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.3N 117.6W
ABOUT 590 MI...950 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...130 MPH...215 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...948 MB...28.00 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Genevieve was
located near latitude 18.3 North, longitude 117.6 West. Genevieve is
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this
general motion with a slight increase in forward speed is expected 
during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 130 mph (215 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Genevieve is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Some fluctuations in intensity are possible 
over the next day or so, and a weakening trend should begin 
thereafter.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 948 mb (28.00 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the 
Baja California Peninsula and will reach Southern California on 
Wednesday. These swells are likely to persist for the next several 
days, and could cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Tue Jul 28 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 290233
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
500 PM HST Tue Jul 28 2026
 
Genevieve's satellite presentation has continued to oscillate this 
afternoon and evening, with deep cold convection wrapping around a 
cloud-filled eye with occasional lightning. A GPM microwave pass 
showed that the western eyewall had started to erode. Over the last 
few hours, there have been occasional breaks within the inner core, 
but the inner core has been resilient and has continued to wrap deep 
convection. Objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS remain 
around 105–118 kt, which prompted the special advisory a few hours 
ago. Using these estimates, the initial intensity is held at 115 kt 
for this advisory.
 
The hurricane will remain in a marginal environment over the next 24 
hours, characterized by low-to-moderate vertical wind shear, sea 
surface temperatures near 27–28C, and mid-level relative humidity 
values in the 50 to 60 percent range. Changes in convective 
organization and inner core dynamics will allow for short-term 
intensity fluctuations over the next day or so. Gradual weakening is 
forecast through 24 hours, followed by a faster rate of decay once 
the system crosses the 26C isotherm in 24–36 hours. As the cyclone 
traverses cooler waters, decreasing mid-level relative humidity will 
further suppress deep convection. The official NHC intensity 
forecast lies near the upper end of the guidance suite in the short 
term, reflecting recent intensity adjustments, and aligns closely 
with the consensus aids from 48 hours through the end of the 
forecast period. The timing of post-tropical transition has been 
moved up to Day 4, consistent with model simulated satellite imagery 
from the latest GFS and ECMWF.

Genevieve is moving west-northwestward at an estimated motion of 
290/8 kt along the southwestern periphery of a ridge centered to the 
northwest of the system. A slightly faster forward speed is 
anticipated during the next few days as the ridge expands westward. 
The NHC track forecast was shifted slightly to the left, and lies 
closest to the HCCA corrected consensus aid.
